related_questions.question: What is the gun control bill in Colorado?

text_blocks.snippet: Colorado recently passed Senate Bill 3, a gun control bill that will significantly restrict the sale and purchase of certain semi-automatic firearms with detachable magazines, effective August 2026. The bill also bans rapid-fire trigger devices like bump stocks. To purchase these firearms, individuals will need to obtain a permit, which requires a background check and safety training.

list.title: Banned Firearms:
list.snippet: Senate Bill 3 bans the manufacture, sale, and purchase of most semi-automatic firearms that can accept detachable magazines. This includes popular models like AR-15s and AK-47s.

list.title: Exceptions:
list.snippet: The bill does not ban firearms that already have fixed, 15-round maximum magazines, which are uncommon. It also exempts law enforcement, military personnel, and others in specific professions.

list.title: Permit Requirement:
list.snippet: Individuals can still purchase the restricted firearms if they obtain a permit.

list.title: Permit Process:
list.snippet: The permit process involves a background check by the county sheriff and completion of a safety course. The length of the course varies (4-12 hours) depending on prior firearms training.

list.title: Rapid-Fire Devices:
list.snippet: The bill also prohibits the sale and purchase of rapid-fire trigger devices like bump stocks.

list.title: Implementation:
list.snippet: The restrictions on sale and purchase take effect in August 2026.
